report.headline: VISTA-16 phase 3 trial of varespladib stopped early for futility; human genetics show PLA2G2A has no causal role in coronary disease (association score 0.0), making target_not_causal the primary failure mode.
report.summary: The VISTA-16 trial randomized 5,189–6,500 acute coronary syndrome patients with metabolic risk factors (triglycerides ≥150 mg/dL, glucose ≥110 mg/dL, blood pressure ≥130/85 mmHg) within 96 hours of onset. The independent DSMB recommended stopping the study on 9 March 2012 due to lack of efficacy, and enrollment was closed with patients removed from therapy. Human genetic evidence gives PLA2G2A a coronary artery disorder association score of 0.0 with zero evidence items, indicating no causal link, and the intended biomarker sPLA2-IIA mass is classified as non-causal. The phase 2 FRANCIS-ACS trial had already shown varespladib reduced LDL-C and inflammatory biomarkers by ~84–87% but produced no difference in clinical cardiovascular events. The calculator predicts expected HR = 1.0 (causal RRR = 0%) because target genetics are not_causal. Confidence in the target_not_causal conclusion is high.
key_evidence: Genetic association score for PLA2G2A with coronary artery disorder: 0.0 (opentargets:PLA2G2A)
Patients randomized: 5,189 participants (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01130246 VISTA-16) / 6,500 patients (Varespladib source)

DSMB recommended stopping VISTA-16 for 'lack of efficacy' on 9 March 2012 (Anthera Halts VISTA-16 Clinical Study Due to Lack of Efficacy Following Recommendation by the Independent Data Safety Monitoring Board)

Phase 2 FRANCIS-ACS: varespladib reduced biomarkers ~84–87% but showed no treatment differences in clinical cardiovascular events (Effects of varespladib methyl on biomarkers and major cardiovascular events in acute coronary syndrome patients)
Calculator expected HR = 1.0, causal RRR = 0% because target genetics are not_causal
report.what_would_change_this: Only evidence of a causal role for PLA2G2A in coronary disease (e.g., Mendelian randomization showing protective effect of loss-of-function variants) would alter the conclusion; the genetic score of 0.0 and futility stop are already definitive.
report.readthrough_note: No read-through hypotheses were generated; other sPLA2-IIA inhibitor programmes would face the same genetic evidence against target causality.

mechanism.notes: VISTA-16 (NCT01130246) was a phase 3 trial stopped early for lack of efficacy (f_d6b498d0939c58, f_f49d7f2e623285). No placebo-adjusted on-treatment biomarker changes from the phase 3 trial are available in the verified facts. Phase 2 biomarker changes exist (e.g., f_1bbee001adb0d2, f_5db4a46719eef0 for 'other' biomarker at 12 weeks; f_aa49aa85cb429e, f_e0d34a84fa8340 for sPLA2-IIA) but are not from the outcome trial, not clearly identified, or not placebo-adjusted. Follow-up duration, event counts, SBP change, and observed HR/CI are not reported in the available facts.

against.text: The DSMB stopped the trial for 'lack of efficacy', not safety; the readout states 'lack of efficacy None'.

for.text: Trial enrolled high-risk ACS patients with metabolic criteria (TG ≥150, glucose ≥110, BP ≥130/85) within 96 hours.

against.text: Phase 2 FRANCIS-ACS in a similar ACS population also showed no clinical event benefit.
Genetic evidence against causality applies broadly, not just to this population.

hypotheses.would_settle: Not a primary explanation; genetics argue against causality in any population.

for.text: Primary endpoint was 'morbidity and mortality' — a standard composite.

against.text: No evidence of endpoint mismatch; the endpoint is appropriate for a cardiovascular outcomes trial.

hypotheses.would_settle: Protocol review would confirm, but no signal of design flaw.

for.text: Trial was stopped early by independent DSMB.

against.text: Stopping for futility per DSMB recommendation is proper trial execution, not a failure of execution.

hypotheses.would_settle: Not a failure mode; execution was appropriate.

for.text: Phase 3 biomarker changes, follow-up duration, event counts, and observed HR/CI are not available in the verified facts.

against.text: Human genetic evidence (score 0.0) and futility stop are sufficient to conclude target_not_causal; missing phase 3 operational data do not change the causal inference.

hypotheses.would_settle: Publication of full trial results would fill gaps but would not alter the genetic conclusion.

issues.issue: Two placebo-adjusted phase 2 biomarker changes from VISTA-16 (f_1bbee001adb0d2: -24% at 12 weeks; f_5db4a46719eef0: -27% at 12 weeks) are labeled only as biomarker "other" in the verified facts. Given these come from the VISTA-16 phase 2 data (pmcid:PMC2653470), they may represent sPLA2-IIA mass/activity changes. If so, they constitute the required placebo-adjusted phase 2 input at the relevant dose (500 mg daily per f_aa49aa85cb429e). The mechanism analyst must clarify what "other" refers to in these records.
issues.request: Search PMC2653470 (VISTA-16 phase 2 publication) to identify the biomarker measured in the placebo-adjusted analyses reporting -24% and -27% changes at 12 weeks. Confirm whether this is sPLA2-IIA mass, sPLA2-IIA activity, or another biomarker.

issues.issue: Calculator input for sPLA2-IIA mass change has null values with method "not measured in available phase 3 facts; phase 2 data exist but are not placebo-adjusted or biomarker-unclear" but no fact_ids cited in the changes array. The automatic check flags missing citation. If the "other" biomarkers above are confirmed as sPLA2-IIA, the changes array should be updated with those values and fact_ids.
issues.request: Once mechanism analyst clarifies the "other" biomarker identity, update the changes array with placebo-adjusted percent change, timepoint (12 weeks), and fact_ids (f_1bbee001adb0d2, f_5db4a46719eef0) if they represent sPLA2-IIA. If not sPLA2-IIA, add fact_ids for the non-placebo-adjusted sPLA2-IIA data (f_aa49aa85cb429e, f_e0d34a84fa8340) to document target engagement.

issues.issue: Follow-up duration and event counts are null in calculator inputs. VISTA-16 was an event-driven trial stopped early for futility. Public sources (ClinicalTrials.gov, press releases) may report planned follow-up, actual median follow-up at stop, or number of primary endpoint events accrued. These are needed for power/MDE calculations even if they don't change the target_not_causal conclusion.
issues.request: Search ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01130246 history, Anthera Pharmaceuticals press releases (March 2012), and any conference presentations for: (a) planned follow-up duration, (b) median follow-up at DSMB stop, (c) number of primary endpoint events at stop, (d) observed HR if reported.
